title: Doubled / Geminate Verbs (Al-Fiʿl al-Muḍāʿaf)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 24; Ryding Ch. 22 §22.3)
objectives: Recognize doubled verbs whose 2nd and 3rd radicals are identical (e.g., مَدَّ, رَدَّ).
Apply the idghām contraction rule: contract with shaddah when C3 is vowelled, separate when C3 carries sukūn.
Conjugate doubled verbs across past, imperfect, and jussive.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 23: Why do Form IX verbs (اِحْمَرَّ) separate their doubled final radical in اِحْمَرَرْتُ?

sections.heading: Gemination (Idghām) vs. Uncontracted Stems
sections.body: A doubled (geminate) verb has identical second and third radicals (e.g., م-د-د → مَدَّ 'to stretch/extend', ر-د-د → رَدَّ 'to return'). When the third radical is followed by a vowel, the two identical consonants merge with shaddah (idghām). When a consonant-initial subject suffix attaches (requiring sukūn on the third radical), the two radicals separate.

sections.label: The Idghām Separation Rule
sections.summary: If C3 is vowelled → contract with shaddah (مَدَّ, مَدُّوا, يَمُدُّ). If C3 has sukūn (before ـْتُ, ـْتَ, ـْنَا, ـْنَ) → separate the radicals (مَدَدْتُ, مَدَدْنَا, يَمْدُدْنَ).

sections.translation: I returned the book to the library.
sections.irab: رَدَدْتُ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ (فُكَّ إِدْغَامُهُ) | التَّاءُ: فَاعِلٌ | الكِتَابَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ
sections.notes: Because ـْتُ begins with a consonant, رَدَّ separates into رَدَدْتُ.

sections.heading: Jussive of Doubled Verbs
sections.body: In the 3ms jussive (لَمْ يَرُدَّ), Classical Arabic commonly keeps the shaddah with fatḥah or kasrah (to avoid a final double consonant), or separates it (لَمْ يَرْدُدْ).
